prompt.context: Your client is a large online retailer, Retailco.com. They sell a wide range of products online from electronics to apparel, etc. They have witnessed strong growth and profitability, however over the last 12 months their operating margins have been thinning. The TV business accounts for a large share of the business and company managers think there is an issue in this division. The CEO has engaged us to identify the cause and make suggestions to improve profitability.
prompt.question: Identify the cause of the thinning operating margins in Retailco.com's TV division and make suggestions to improve profitability.

clarifying_info.q: What type of retailer is Retailco.com?
clarifying_info.a: Retailco.com is a major online retailer that sells all types of products (think like Amazon.com) directly to consumers in the United States.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific profitability target or timeline?
clarifying_info.a: No particular target ROI or profitability. ASAP action needed.
Shipping product from a warehouse in the same region in which the order was placed (e.g., servicing a Mid-West customer order from a Mid-West warehouse).
Shipping product from a warehouse in a different region (e.g., servicing a Mid-West customer order from a West Coast warehouse).

exhibits.title: Average cost structure of a TV sold by Retailco ($)
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the average cost per TV sold across four years (2015, 2016, 2017, 2018). Costs are broken into four components: COGS, Shipping, Holding, and Other. The y-axis runs from 0 to 90 dollars.

data.note: Exact per-year values must be read from the chart; shipping cost visibly increases from approximately $15 in 2017 to $20 in 2018; other cost components (COGS, Holding, Other) appear relatively stable across years

exhibits.title: TV units shipped by region type (%)
exhibits.shows: A 100% stacked bar chart comparing the share of TV units shipped in-region vs. out-region for 2017 and 2018. Total TVs shipped equals 100,000 units.

data.note: The split between in-region and out-region shipments changed between 2017 and 2018; exact percentages must be read from the chart

framework: Check revenue: revenue is not the issue; growth has been strong
Check costs: identify major cost categories for an online retailer (COGS, shipping, holding/warehousing, marketing, returns/damages, overhead)
Isolate the cost driver: shipping costs have increased significantly from 2017 to 2018 while other costs are stable
Diagnose the shipping cost increase: brainstorm reasons (carrier rate hikes, larger package sizes, longer shipping distances / out-region mix shift)
Quantify the mix shift impact and evaluate solutions to reduce out-region shipping
Recommend: hold more in-region inventory (up to the break-even holding weeks) to convert out-region shipments to in-region

questions.prompt: Walk through the major cost categories for an online retailer and identify which has increased.
questions.guidance: Candidate should systematically list cost buckets: COGS, shipping, warehousing/holding, marketing/customer acquisition, returns and damages, overhead. After brainstorming, Exhibit 1 is shared. Candidate must read the chart and note that shipping cost rises from ~$15/TV in 2017 to ~$20/TV in 2018 while all other line items are flat. This identifies shipping as the sole driver.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm reasons why shipping costs may have increased over the last year.
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover at least three buckets: (1) Carrier rate increases (FedEx, UPS raised base rates), (2) Package characteristics (larger or heavier TVs, dimensional weight pricing), (3) Distance / regional mix shift (more shipments traveling longer distances, i.e., out-region shipping has grown). The interviewer should push toward the third reason before sharing Exhibit 2.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, quantify how the regional shipping mix changed from 2017 to 2018 and explain the cost impact.
questions.guidance: Candidate should extract: 2017 = 80K in-region, 20K out-region; 2018 = 60K in-region, 40K out-region. Out-region shipments doubled (20K to 40K). Given in-region rate = $10/TV and out-region rate = $35/TV, calculate the average shipping cost per TV for each year and confirm this matches the Exhibit 1 increase.

math.setup: Weighted average shipping cost = (in-region units × $10 + out-region units × $35) / total units
math.answer: Average shipping cost rose from $15/TV to $20/TV, entirely explained by the out-region mix shift (out-region share doubled from 20% to 40%).

questions.prompt: How many additional weeks of inventory can Retailco.com justify holding in warehouses to avoid out-region shipping?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare the cost of holding extra inventory (holding cost) against the savings from avoiding an out-region shipment. Difference in shipping cost = $35 - $10 = $25 per TV. Holding cost = $5 per TV per week. Break-even = $25 / $5 = 5 weeks. The retailer can justify holding up to 5 additional weeks of inventory rather than shipping out-region.

math.setup: Break-even holding weeks = (out-region rate - in-region rate) / holding cost per week
steps: Savings per TV by converting out-region to in-region = $35 - $10 = $25
Holding cost = $5 per TV per week
math.answer: Retailco.com can hold up to 5 additional weeks of inventory and still be cost-neutral vs. shipping out-region.

brainstorming.prompt: What actions could Retailco.com take to shift more shipments to in-region and reduce out-region shipping?

categories.name: Inventory placement and forecasting
ideas: Improve demand forecasting by region to pre-position inventory closer to customers
Hold more weeks of inventory in regional warehouses (up to the 5-week break-even threshold)
Analyze historical regional sales patterns to optimize stock distribution across warehouses

categories.name: Warehouse network
ideas: Open new fulfillment centers in underserved regions to reduce out-region distance
Partner with third-party logistics providers to gain regional capacity without capital investment
Use micro-fulfillment or dark stores in high-density metro areas

categories.name: Supplier and procurement
ideas: Negotiate with TV suppliers to deliver directly to regional warehouses rather than a central hub
Work with manufacturers on regional allocation agreements tied to historical demand

categories.name: Technology and operations
ideas: Implement real-time inventory visibility to route orders to nearest stocked warehouse
Use machine-learning demand planning tools to reduce forecast error by region
Set minimum in-region stock level alerts before accepting new orders in a region

recommendation: Shipping costs have increased from $15 to $20 per TV driven entirely by a doubling of out-region shipments (20K to 40K units) as the share of out-region orders rose from 20% to 40%

Retailco.com should hold more inventory in regional warehouses — up to 5 additional weeks of stock — to convert out-region shipments to in-region, since the holding cost savings ($5/week) break even at exactly 5 weeks vs. the $25/TV premium for out-region shipping
This will restore average shipping cost toward $15/TV and recover approximately $5/TV in margin across the TV division
risks: Holding more inventory increases working capital requirements and warehouse space costs
If demand forecasts are inaccurate, excess regional inventory may result in markdowns or write-offs
Macro events (supply chain disruptions, demand spikes) could make regional pre-positioning less effective
Competitor pricing pressure or carrier rate hikes could erode savings even after mix correction
next_steps: Conduct a region-by-region demand analysis to determine optimal inventory levels per warehouse
Model the working capital and storage cost impact of holding up to 5 additional weeks of TV inventory
Evaluate warehouse capacity and identify whether new facilities or third-party partnerships are needed
Implement improved demand forecasting tools to reduce reliance on reactive out-region shipping
Monitor in-region vs. out-region split monthly with a target to return to at least 80% in-region by end of year
